title: Do VLAs Know They Will Fail? Interpretable Success and Failure Patterns in Physical AI Systems
abstract: arXiv:2610.32208v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have emerged as powerful general-purpose robot policies, but their successes and failures remain difficult to diagnose and understand. In this work, we show that sparse autoencoder (SAE) representations of OpenVLA activations contain outcome-predictive information and can be used to predict task failure before the robot reaches an unrecoverable state. Moreover, to provide insights into what common behaviors may contribute to these outcomes, we identify individual SAE features whose strong activations are associated with specific stages of success or failure, and uncover recurring behavioral patterns by localizing temporal intervals where these features exhibit significant activation changes. We further develop a VLM-based interpretation pipeline to generate behavioral descriptions of these patterns and validate their correspondence to feature activations on held-out intervals.

translated_title: VLA模型知道自己会失败吗？物理AI系统中可解释的成功与失败模式
translated_abstract: 视觉-语言-动作（VLA）模型已成为强大的通用机器人策略，但其成功与失败仍然难以诊断和理解。在这项工作中，我们展示了OpenVLA激活的稀疏自编码器（SAE）表示包含可预测结果的信息，可用于在机器人进入不可恢复状态之前预测任务失败。此外，为了深入洞察哪些常见行为可能导致这些结果，我们识别了强激活与成功或失败特定阶段相关联的个体SAE特征，并通过定位这些特征表现出显著激活变化的时间区间，揭示了反复出现的行为模式。我们进一步开发了一个基于VLM的解释流程，为这些模式生成行为描述，并在保留的时间区间上验证了其与特征激活的对应关系。
tldr: 本论文发现OpenVLA激活的稀疏自编码器（SAE）表示蕴含结果预测信息，可在机器人任务陷入不可恢复状态前预测失败，并通过识别与成败阶段相关的SAE特征及基于VLM的解释流程，揭示反复出现的行为模式。
en_tdlr: This paper shows that sparse autoencoder representations of OpenVLA activations contain outcome-predictive information enabling early failure prediction, and identifies individual SAE features linked to success/failure stages to uncover recurring behavioral patterns via a VLM-based interpretation pipeline.
